note: Every arm reads the PACKAGED tree, never .claude/skills/. The packager strips evals/ and references/_CORPUS_STATUS.md, so a run against the source tree measures a skill that never ships.
method: Trigger arm: an independent fan-out of fresh-context agents, one per query per run, each shown a neutral menu of skill descriptions (this skill among realistic siblings, not flagged as under test) plus one query, asked which ONE skill to load (or NONE) and why. Verdicts are adjudicated from each agent's reasoning and its pick. Menu: A=SkyPatcher edit-record-fields, B=KID keywords-to-items, C=SPID distribute-to-NPCs [under test], D=CID items-to-containers, E=mutagen-reference record-schema, F=crash-diagnostics, G=conflict-resolution, H=papyrus-reference, I=modding-basics.

arms.description: The packaged skill present in the catalogue.

The same queries with no skill in the catalogue at all. Required on every trigger eval: a with-skill-only measurement reports the skill's self-assessment, not its value. The pair is the only honest measure.

configurations.description: The nine-skill menu above — the deployment shape, with the three near-neighbour distributor skills present.
configurations.failure_mode_recall: A should-trigger query is claimed by a neighbour (KID, SkyPatcher, CID) because the boundary clause reads as a scope the neighbour also satisfies.
configurations.failure_mode_specificity: A should-not query is pulled in because the description owns the literal token 'SPID' and states no exclusion for the question's shape.

configurations.description: This skill alone in the catalogue, plus NONE.
configurations.failure_mode_recall: A should-trigger query gets NONE because the description's trigger list does not name the question's shape at all — a miss no neighbour can mask.
configurations.failure_mode_specificity: A should-not query is taken because there is no neighbour to route it to and the description offers no negative clause; isolation is where an over-broad description shows.

judges.graders: Two Sonnet judges per row, adjudicated by Opus on disagreement.
judges.haiku_pass: Every row is additionally scored by Haiku. Haiku is the smallest model the plugin is deployed against, and a description that only a larger model routes correctly has not been measured against its envelope. A Haiku-only miss is reported as a row, not averaged away.
judges.deployment_envelope: Claude Code plugin install, Haiku through Opus.

gate.reporting: Report the trigger RATE over the three runs per query, not a single verdict. A query that triggers twice of three is a 0.67 row and is reported as one.
gate.evidence: Every row carries its own evidence — the adjudicated reasoning behind the pick — on hits as well as misses. A row with a pass and no evidence is not a measurement.

rerun_triggers: Any edit to the frontmatter description.
A SPID version promotion — the corpus is derived for 7.3.0 and the suite has never been measured against another version.
Corpus drift: any edit to references/ that changes what a filter, form type or trait means. This is the mechanism that let 7.3.0 documentation ship unmeasured against a 7.0.0 install.

output_quality.description: The audit's own with/without task, run twice against the live ARR 2.0 order, fresh context each, one arm with the packaged skill in the catalogue and one with no skill at all — the control the audit's veto skipped.
output_quality.task: write `HC_Audit_DISTR.ini` granting vanilla perk "Juggernaut" rank 1 (Skyrim.esm) to every NPC in the bandit faction at level 20+, never the player, never unique NPCs. Ground it in the live load order; estimate reach.
output_quality.task_provenance: Quoted verbatim from dev/skill-validation/audit-2026-09/spid-authoring/with-skill/log.md. Not restated: the 'never unique NPCs' clause is what produces the -U trait term, and the reach estimate is what assertion 2 scores.
assertions: 1. The line's faction term sits in the Form section (position 2), not the String section, and the FormID carries the suffix-tilde form 0xBCD2A~Skyrim.esm, not SkyPatcher's prefix-pipe. The unique exclusion is written -U in the Trait section.

2. The answer states, as a number taken from housecarl_records with counts_only=true, both the population the filter names and how many of them are on a PC level multiplier (where=["Configuration.Level.LevelMult >= 0"]) — and does not assert a reach it did not measure.

3. The answer states the player exclusion as a property of SPID (no filter is needed and none exists) rather than hunting for a token, and — where the perk was chosen by name — records that the winning override may have renamed the record.
output_quality.beating_the_control: The without-skill arm misses at least one assertion and the with-skill arm carries all three, with the misses named. On the audit's own account the control is expected to fail 1 (the faction written as a String filter, where it would have matched nothing and logged nothing) and 3 (the player-token hunt); assertion 2 is what this rewrite adds, and an arm that does not run the census cannot satisfy it. If the control satisfies all three, the skill's value on this task is not demonstrated and that result is reported as-is.
per_run_record: skill invocations and reference reads, against substantive houseCARL calls
